claims.text: Rapidly quenched Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 can contain an amorphous phase.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has a broad solidification range and complex crystallization behavior.
Rapidly quenched Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has only limited amorphous formation or retention.
Rapidly quenched Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 tends to crystallize early during reheating.
Cooling Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 at approximately 3000 K/s can promote amorphization.
A short isothermal hold 50–100 K below the crystallization onset is necessarily a sub-Tg treatment.
A secondary quench after the hold will freeze the structurally relaxed state.
The post-quench hold will promote atomic-scale structural relaxation.
The post-quench hold will reduce internal stresses in the amorphous matrix.
The post-quench hold will decrease excess free volume in the amorphous matrix.
During the proposed hold, atoms can rearrange into a lower-energy configuration without crystallizing.
Structural relaxation and reduced free volume will lower the driving force for crystallization.
A post-quench sub-Tg hold will improve amorphous retention during solidification relative to rapid quenching alone.
The treated alloy will have a higher amorphous fraction after processing than a rapid-quench-only control.
The treated alloy will show delayed or reduced exothermic crystallization during DSC reheating.
Holding too close to the crystallization temperature or for too long may cause partial crystallization.
An insufficient initial cooling rate may prevent formation of an amorphous precursor and limit the benefit of the hold.
The optimal hold temperature and duration for Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 are not yet specified.

contradictions.description: The intervention occurs immediately after rapid quenching and thus after the initial solidification history, yet it is claimed to improve amorphous retention during solidification and to increase the fraction produced by that initial solidification.

A temperature 50–100 K below crystallization onset is labeled sub-Tg, but the hypothesis does not establish Tg or show that this temperature is below Tg; being below crystallization onset is not by itself equivalent to being below Tg.
